notes:
Account overview: EchoRelay Labs builds an AI-native outbound SDR product used by mid-market SaaS companies. Primary goal is to add a low-latency streaming chat agent that can take actions in Salesforce, send personalized emails through Gmail, and schedule meetings with Calendar integrations. They prefer starting on Redwood Hosted API for speed to value, but want a clear path to Dedicated/VPC once throughput and data isolation needs are validated.

Key requirements (from product/eng):
- Streaming token-level responses (UI shows tokens as they arrive)
- Function/tool-calling orchestration: SFDC create/update, Gmail send/draft, Calendar create/accept
- Latency SLO: p50 per-token <= 120ms in production; p95 target <= 200-250ms for typical convo lengths
- Throughput target for initial Dedicated sizing: ~40 concurrent active agents, bursting to 120 with autoscale
- Cost sensitivity: wants to compare hosted per-token cost vs committed Dedicated pricing; likely 12-month commit if unit economics favorable
- Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML, KMS-managed keys for any stored artifacts, audit logs retention 13 months, potential EU data residency for some customers

POC specifics: 3-week technical POC run by EchoRelay eng with Redwood SE (Maya). Scope: implement tool-calling flows, measure end-to-end latency, test streaming UX across mobile web, run failure/fallback tests (simulate model OOMs, forced fallbacks to quantized variant). EchoRelay will provide a small corpus of prompts and 250 canonical customer scenarios.

Quotes/voice of customer: "We need the chat to feel instant — even small token delays kill conversion in the UI." — Head of Product.

Commercial: Initial pricing conversation happening; echoing finance wants ARR range estimate and a Dedicated sizing worksheet. AE to deliver Dedicated pricing + break-even analysis vs hosted.

Open items / risks: VPC peering constraints on EchoRelay AWS account (security team flagged outbound IP allowlist), need clear KMS key rotation policy from Redwood, budget owner (VP GTM) out on leave until 2026-03-25 which may push procurement.

Attachments: pricing draft, security Q&A, Fireflies links (see linked_fireflies).
